newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's El Abra fixes belt, now at full capacity.
newsitem.headline: Chile's El Abra fixes belt, now at full capacity.

text.p: Chile's El Abra copper mine has fixed a conveyor belt damaged in a serious accident last month and is working at full capacity, said site manager John Fenn.
"The conveyor belt was back in operation on November 1," Fenn told Reuters by telephone from the pit.
Asked if the 225,000-tonne mine was now working at full capacity, Fenn replied: "Yes."
El Abra, which cast its first cathode in August, is 51-percent owned by Cyprus Amax Minerals with 49 percent held by state copper company Codelco.
Company officials have said that the accident will cut production this year to 58,000 tonnes, 9,000 tonnes less than originally planned.

Four workers died at the mine in October when a tunnel covering the conveyor belt linking the open-cast pit and the heap-leaching plant collapsed burying them under tonnes of rocks and debris. -- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595x212
